title: A pinned image with the test films, for a client's CI
description: A client that tests against jellyscale (Fluster first, issue #160) needs a published image it can pin, the films jellyscale's own tests use, and a start with a known user and library. Today the Dockerfile is built by nobody but the dogfood's manual redeploy, into a private registry, with no version tag, and CI never runs the image. This task publishes the server image and a '-fixtures' image with a small synthetic library baked in, from a workflow on GitHub-hosted runners, tested before each push.
acceptanceCriteria: test/fixtures/client.sh <dir> makes the client library with synthetic names only: make.sh's films and episodes, plus 'Babel Film' (audio 1 eng default, 2 deu, 3 fra, 4 untagged; subtitles 5 eng, 6 eng forced, 7 eng SDH, 8 deu, 9 ger forced, 10 fra, 11 untagged, 12 jpn PGS; beside it .de.srt and .es.srt) and 'Kino Film' (audio 1 deu default, 2 eng; subtitles 3 deu, 4 eng, 5 fra), as JS-119 lists them. One recipe makes each film for this script and for jellyscale's own checks. The result is under 300 MB

The Dockerfile builds two targets: the server, and 'fixtures', which is the server plus client.sh's films under /fixtures/media and a config naming the libraries and adminUser 'test'. The fixtures image starts as --roles=all with that config by default, with no volume, no init container and no web client, and holds no password: without JELLYSCALE_ADMIN_PASSWORD it stops at start saying so
Both images carry org.opencontainers.image.revision (the commit), .version and .source, and the two images of one build carry the same revision

deploy/fixtures/compose.yaml starts Postgres and the fixtures image named by JELLYSCALE_IMAGE (required, no default), with the server's port published on 127.0.0.1 at a port Docker assigns and Postgres published nowhere; `docker compose up -d --wait` returns when GET /readyz answers 200

test/image.sh [image] builds both targets (or pulls the image named), starts that compose file, reads the port with `docker compose port`, signs in as 'test', and within 60 s finds the documented number of films and episodes. It then checks: Babel Film's PlaybackInfo lists 15 streams with the documented type, language and codec at each index, and Kino Film's 6; a byte range of a direct-play film answers 206; the first segment of a transcode of the AC3 film holds H.264 video and AAC audio (the image's own ffmpeg made it); Babel Film's English text track as VTT has its first cue. It fails when Docker is missing, never skips, and leaves no container, network or volume behind, also after a kill

A workflow, on ubuntu-24.04 hosted runners only, on every push to main and every tag vX.Y.Z: builds both targets, runs test/image.sh on them, and only then pushes those same images to ghcr.io/jellyscale-org/jellyscale with the job's own token (packages: write on that job alone) as main-<12 hex> and main-<12 hex>-fixtures, and for a tag also X.Y.Z and X.Y.Z-fixtures. A release tag that already exists in the registry is never overwritten: the run fails naming it. No latest. A test of the workflow file fails on a self-hosted or larger-runner label and on a push step that does not need the test step
After the merge, from a machine not logged in to the registry: `docker pull` of the commit's -fixtures tag succeeds and test/image.sh passes against the pulled image

docs/client-testing.md (new, linked from README and docs/running.md) gives the image name and the two kinds of tag, the compose start, the user, a wait loop for the scan, every film by name with its tracks by index, how to make the films without the image, that item ids are looked up by name, and that the fixtures image is for tests only. A test fails when the page's film list, user name, compose path or counts differ from what test/image.sh checks
CONTRIBUTING.md says how a release is cut: a tag vX.Y.Z on a commit of main whose image run passed, and a GitHub release with generated notes
ci.yml's four required checks and their run time are unchanged; the image workflow is not a required check
notes: Independent of the track-language tasks: it builds side by side with JS-118. If it lands before JS-119, it makes the Babel and Kino recipes and JS-119's checks use them; if after, it reuses JS-119's. Make the films on the runner with CI's ffmpeg (test/apt.sh) and copy them into the image, so the recipes run under the ffmpeg the tests use; alpine's ffmpeg then only has to play them, which test/image.sh shows. A second, non-administrator viewer waits for JS-033; no seeding route or flag is added (the app must not know it is tested). The password is in the compose file, not the image. Owner steps: make the ghcr.io package public once; decide the first version tag. The dogfood's private build is untouched. Merged as #164 (2026-11-16); the first image run published main-48c17716d578 and -fixtures. Open: the pull from a machine not logged in waits for the owner to make the ghcr.io package public.
